$sources: Sections of the Tianqing case's monochromes (Ding, Jun, Guan, Jian, Longquan): the turned outlines as the stage's sheet gives them (Docs/Stages/chenghuai.md, section 8: 'ceramics from the catalogue, turned profiles windows/SourceArt/Textures/ch_vessels.json scaled to them'), each traced from the Metropolitan Museum's open-access photograph of a vessel of its type (windows/Scripts/chenghuai_vessels.py): [radius, height] in metres from the centre of the foot, out along the underside, up the outside, over the lip and down the inside to the axis, the solid on the left. Art scales each to the plan's size (the catalogue's).

Sections of the Changnan case's vessels and the Ru basin (grade 'derived'): derived from each vessel's own photographs in the collection (assets/ceramics/<work>/, credited in its CREDITS.md) by MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py, each vessel's derivation written in its record: the silhouette against its plain ground, the camera fitted to the rim's and foot's ellipses (correcting the photograph's perspective), scaled to the museum's height and checked against its published diameter; the underside and inside by Data/Art/Ware.json's wall rule. `museum` is the museum's record of the vessel's size; `outside` the section's first and last points of its outside.

Views (a painted vessel's): each photograph's camera as the derivation found it (bearing from the vessel's front towards its right, distance from its axis and height above its foot in metres, pitch down, focal length and optical axis in the photograph's pixels); a further view is placed by registering its painting on the others' where they overlap. Bands: the painted bands of ornament and their repeat, found by the autocorrelation of each band's painting where the views see it, rounded to a whole number of repeats a turn.

Stand: the carved phoebe stand a vessel stands on where its plan says `stand`, as the sheet gives it (Data/Stages/chenghuai/Hang.json, the cases' notes: radius 1.25 x the foot, 0.028 high under a vessel 0.20 tall, else 0.04), in the case's phoebe (Data/Stages/chenghuai/Finishes.json chenghuai.case.phoebe).

creaseDegrees: a section known only by its traced points turns smoothly where it turns less than 20 degrees from one point to the next and keeps an arris where it turns more (the lip's and the foot ring's edges): the museum's rule for a path known only by its points (Form's kernel, Tolerances.h, CreaseAngleRadians, from the as-built museum).

Composition (Art, Vessel/VesselDecoration.h): a view lends its colour where it sees the surface within 60 degrees of face on (squarenessCut 0.5: beyond it one pixel of the photograph covers more than twice the surface it does face on, a stretch the painting wouldn't bear), its weight rising as the square from there to face on. Each photograph is divided by its white: its hue that of the samples within 5 per cent of the 0.9 quantile of the lightness it shows where it sees the outside within 37 degrees of face on (whiteSquareness 0.8: a painted porcelain's ground is its glaze, most of what a view sees there); its lightness a plane in the surface's normal fitted to the plain glaze it shows (samples whose channels spread no more than a quarter of their largest, glazeChroma 0.25, and no darker than 0.4 of its white, glazeLightness), taking off the photograph's shading, never below 0.2 of the white (shadeFloor). A sample 1.15 times its white is the lamp's reflection in the glaze, lent at 0.05 of its weight. The views alone give the colour from a summed weight of 0.04 (one view within 53 degrees of face on), a band's repeats or the glaze filling in below it. The decoration is composed at up to 16000 px a metre, the finest the collection's photographs resolve (the chicken cup's), and at most 8192 px across (Art's WorkImageMaxPixels).

Check: widest diameter 48.5 cm (museum 48.3 cm). Underside and inside by Data/Art/Ware.json's wall rule. MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py. Decoration: each further view placed by registering its painting, unwrapped round the axis, on the others' where they overlap (turn and height, then its camera refined on the painting); the views see 28% of the outside within 60 degrees of face on; where none does, each band's own repeat is carried round from where it is best seen, and elsewhere the glaze is left.

vessels.source: National Palace Museum, Taipei, 故瓷017851, narcissus basin, Ru ware: H. 6.9 cm; mouth 23.0 x 16.4 cm; foot 19.3 x 12.9 cm (the order K9 table)
vessels.derivation: Section derived from the museum's sizes and the proportions the oblique photograph 汝窯_青瓷無紋水仙盆.png shows at the basin's left end, read by eye on its pixel grid (MuseeVision/Scripts/vessels.py, RU): feet 0.13, flange 0.20 and wall 0.67 of the height; the flange's face the museum's foot, the wall stepping in 2.2 mm above it and flaring to the mouth; the wall Data/Art/Ware.json's. No photograph shows the section edge on, so no camera is fitted: the photograph's foreshortening falls on every height alike and cancels in the shares. Turned in the round on the long half-axis and pressed front to back to the mouth's 23.0 x 16.4 cm, its foot comes to 19.3 x 13.8 cm against the museum's 19.3 x 12.9 (a wall that flared as far at the ends as at the sides would give 12.7 across the short axis). Four feet from the base photograph. Glaze colour from the lit outside wall, face on (pixels 1100..1500 x 1350..1500), relative to the photograph's white.
